bri: Heads up — finance pushed back on the Q4 burst budget. They want concrete numbers to justify a 3-month committed burst pool in eu-west. Anyone got a defensible forecast we can use in the SOW?

soumya: We ran a few demand scenarios this morning. Quick summary: baseline, optimistic (enterprise onramp), and spike (new customer cohort +marketing). I can paste the top-line metrics.

soumya: ```
scenario: baseline | peak_rps: 850 | est_gpu_hours_month: 12k
scenario: optimistic | peak_rps: 1.4k | est_gpu_hours_month: 20k
scenario: spike | peak_rps: 2.6k | est_gpu_hours_month: 36k
```

alex: Nice. For a 3mo committed burst pool we should size for optimistic but include an automatic scale-down trigger. Procurement will hate overcommit.

james: @soumya can you also break that down by model class (small-gen, large-gen, embeddings)? procurement needs cost per workload for negotiation.

soumya: Yep. Rough split today is 55% large-gen (H100-like), 30% embeddings (A10-ish), 15% small-gen. Attaching quick numbers inline: large-gen 11k gpu-hrs, embeddings 5k, small-gen 4k in optimistic.

lia: From product: we have two launch criteria tied to this: 1) 99.9% uptime for hosted API, and 2) p95 gen latency < 250ms for small-gen and < 550ms for large-gen under steady traffic. Any committed pool has to guarantee those SLOs or we throttle.

procurement-bot: Purchase request draft created: PR-2026-BURST. Link: https://internal.redwood/pr/PR-2026-BURST (status: draft).

alex: If procurement gets a 3mo commit, propose a clause: we get the right to pause burst for non-critical traffic during stocked maintenance windows. That lowers $ penalty risk.

bri: Finance is asking for an ROI rationale — tie burst to predicted ARR uplift from the new feature. Do we have a short note?

james: Short: conservative uplift of 1.8% ARR from product launch in Q4 if we avoid throttling outages during spikes. I can formalize with dollar numbers, but need expected conversions from PM.

lia: PMs gave conservative conversion lift = 0.9–2.5% range. Use 1.2% as mid for procurement negotiations.

alex: Also propose a hybrid contract: baseline reserved capacity (1yr) + 3mo burst add-on (commit tiered by GPU-hours). That way we lock lower unit price on baseline and keep optionality.

soumya: One more technical ask: if we sign burst with vendor X they only guarantee baseline throughput for 1s windows. Our continuous-batching runtime needs per-token KV cache locality across requests — will that be impacted if traffic shifts between hosts? We should add a 99% affinity SLA.

lia: Good point — product can relax strict latency for embeddings in the spike window but gen endpoints must keep affinity. Add that to launch checklist.

bri: Action items: Soumya — send per-model GPU-hr breakdown + cost scenarios by EOD; James — draft ROI paragraph with dollarized uplift; Alex — work a contract outline with procurement and include pause windows + affinity SLA; Lia — update launch criteria doc to include affinity and throttling policy. I'll loop in @finance once we have numbers. :thumbsup:

soumya: Will do. Posting the spreadsheet snippet here as a quick calc: 
```
opt_peak_gpu_hours = {large:11000, embed:5000, small:4000}
opt_monthly_cost_est = sum(opt_peak_gpu_hours[g]*unit_cost[g] for g in GPU_TYPES)
```

james: I'll mock dollar uplift using 1.2% mid. If anyone needs the sheet, ping me and I'll share.

alex: Reminder — vendor lead times are 6–8 weeks for additional nodes, so contract needs a 4–6 week buffer for capacity turn-up. Call that out in SOW.

procurement-bot: PR-2026-BURST updated with lead-time note. New status: review.

bri: Great. If there are no objections, I'm going to present this hybrid sizing + ROI framing to finance tomorrow morning. Minor follow-ups in thread after that.

lia: No objections from product. Thanks everyone.

soumya: I'll drop the detailed numbers in the thread in ~2h.
